public_headline: Helicopter Crew Reports UAP Near Reagan National Airport in 2023
public_tldr: This FAA document is an operational notification from the Washington Operations Center recording a UAP sighting by a helicopter crew on 1 February 2023. The helicopter, callsign FFX1, was orbiting at 1,200 feet about 8 miles southwest of Reagan National Airport when the crew spotted an unidentified aerial phenomenon off the left side of the aircraft. No evasive action was taken, and the National Capital Region Coordination Center was notified.
public_narrative:
On 1 February 2023 at 7:59 PM Eastern, the FAA's Washington Operations Center logged an incident notification: a helicopter crew had reported seeing something they could not identify in the sky near Washington, DC. The document is a short operational alert, not a full investigation.

The helicopter, flying under the callsign FFX1, was orbiting at 1,200 feet roughly 8 miles southwest of Reagan National Airport (DCA), near coordinates 38.76°N, 77.13°W. The crew reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon visible from the left side of the aircraft. The record notes that no evasive action was taken.

The FAA notified the National Capital Region Coordination Center (NCRCC), the body responsible for airspace security around the capital. The document does not describe what the object looked like, how it moved, or how long it was visible.

There is no follow-up investigation, resolution, or conclusion recorded in this document. It is a single preliminary notification — a record that the sighting was reported and that the relevant authority was informed, nothing more.
public_caveats: This is a preliminary operational notification, not an investigation report. It contains no analysis or conclusions about what the crew observed.
No description of the UAP's appearance, size, behaviour, or movement is provided anywhere in the document.
The report comes from a single helicopter crew. No corroborating observations from radar, other aircraft, or ground witnesses are mentioned.
The document contains no follow-up details — there is no indication whether the sighting was ever investigated further.
Redaction levels are low, but the document is inherently limited in scope: it was designed to log and escalate, not to explain.
